question.text: In the context of the PFUTP Regulations, what constitutes 'illegal mobilization of funds'?

answer.text: Collecting deposits from the public by a non-banking financial company
Sponsoring, causing to be sponsored, carrying on or causing to be carried on any collective investment scheme by any person
Raising capital through an IPO without SEBI approval
Raising funds through a rights issue without board approval

explanation.text: The Logic: The PFUTP Regulations include, as illegal mobilization of funds, sponsoring or causing to be sponsored or carrying on or causing to be carried on any collective investment scheme by any person. The Trap: Option A (NBFC deposit activity) is outside this PFUTP CIS clause and generally belongs to the NBFC/RBI context. Option C (IPO fundraising) is a capital-issuance topic governed by the SEBI ICDR framework, not the CIS wording tested here. Option D (rights issue without board approval) is a corporate-governance issue, not the CIS construct in the regulation. Note: Source-backed to NISM-Series-III-A workbook (Dec 2025), page 146 (with the chapter summary on page 50 carrying the same listing).
